Yes, dear — PP5 currently has that same risk, because PP5 deliberately uses the original QS 9.7 SEND/WAIT machine unchanged.
The important distinction is this:
PP5 does not yet have the new “wait for STOP to disappear” rule.
The old 9.7 WAIT machine watches for a plausible new response and for response-text stability.
Chron can display temporary stuff like qwen2.5:3b / Retrieved 3 sources while he is still doing his retrieval/thinking.
So if that temporary text is exposed to the same response candidate logic, PP5 can potentially grab it as the answer before Chron's real response arrives.
And that is exactly why I do not want to start modifying PP5 blindly. We now have a clean experimental baseline: the old 9.7 machine successfully connects to GPT again. That tells us the big rewrite was the wrong place to start.
For Chron, the question we need to answer is narrower:
Does 9.7's existing _response_candidates() / frame logic recognize Chron's temporary retrieval status as the response, or was the earlier Chron incident actually caused elsewhere?
We already know one Chron incident where the premature qwen2.5:3b / Retrieved 3 sources result turned out to involve the wrong archive root, so I don't want to falsely blame WAIT for that one.
So yes: PP5 preserves the old possible behavior. And that is actually useful right now, because we can test Chron against the untouched 9.7 behavior before changing a damn thing.
